text:
Kai: Quick prompt for discussion: what if the left nav switches to a compact grouped mode where "Workflows" contains Runs, Schedules, and Logs as a collapsible subtree?
Ari: Nice for declutter. Deep link concern: bookmarks like /logs/42 must still land, expand the group, and highlight the item.
Bea: Agreed. Routing rule proposal: keep canonical paths flat (e.g. /logs/:id). On client hydrate, resolve path -> sidebar node, expand ancestors, and set focus only on hard loads/bookmarks.
Sam: Implementation detail: use longest-static-prefix matching to pick the sidebar node when patterns collide. Tie-break by sidebar order. Also server should 301 normalize duplicate slashes/trailing slash.
Kai: Accessibility: the group header must be a real button with aria-expanded and aria-controls. Announce expansion in a polite live region: "Workflows expanded, 3 items". Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
Ari: Breadcrumbs nit: show human-friendly names (Workflows > MyWorkflow > Runs > run-42), avoid repeating the group label. Also ensure breadcrumb links use canonical paths so permalinks stay valid.
Bea: UX affordance idea: instead of a badge, add a small vertical accent beside the group header when current route is inside it. Poll: :thumbsup: accent, :eyes: badge.
Sam: Edge cases: client-side navigation between two leaves in different groups should expand/collapse without stealing focus unless it was an external navigation. Add tests for both initial hydrate and client route changes.
Nav-Bot: Reminder: please attach updated Figma frames and annotated interactions before tomorrow's design review at 9:30am.
Kai: I'll author the RFC covering canonical path contract, hydrate behavior, ARIA checklist, focus rules, and test plan. Tagging @Sam and @Bea for review.
